title: Plants, Animals, and Habitats
intro: Sort bean evidence, pollen and seed helpers, and habitat picture sets.
note: This is a sorting game model that uses the lesson's backup data. The real bean investigation and the Seed or Pollen Mover Model still count.
summary: Beans with sunlight and water grew green and sturdy. Without sunlight they were pale, thin and flopped over, and without water they stayed small and dry. Bees and other animals can move pollen, and animals and burrs can move seeds. The forest picture set had 6 kinds of living things and the dune set had 3.

stages.prompt: Bean plants grew for 14 days. Which plants had which results?

cards.label: Green, 4 leaves
cards.why: With sun and water the beans were green with 4 leaves and grew to 9 paper clips by day 14.
cards.hint: what do the color and the number of leaves tell you the plant got?

cards.label: 9 clips tall, strong
cards.why: The beans with sun and water reached 9 paper clips on day 14 and stayed green.
cards.hint: does it look tall and healthy?

cards.label: Pale yellow, thin
cards.why: Without sun the beans still grew, but they were pale yellow and thin.
cards.hint: what does a pale yellow, thin plant tell you?

cards.label: Flops over, 2 leaves
cards.why: The beans grown in the dark flopped over and had only 2 leaves.
cards.hint: look at the leaves and how the plant stands.

cards.label: In the sun, stayed 1 clip
cards.why: With no water the beans stayed 1 paper clip tall.
cards.hint: did this plant grow at all?

cards.label: In the sun, dry brown
cards.why: Without water the beans dried out and turned brown.
cards.hint: look at the color and how dry it is.

stages.prompt: Does this move pollen, or does it move seeds?

cards.label: Bee on a flower
cards.why: A bee carries pollen from flower to flower.
cards.hint: Is it flower powder, or a seed taking a ride?

cards.label: Yellow cornmeal moved
cards.why: In the model, cornmeal moves from flower to flower like pollen.
cards.hint: is this flower powder, or a seed taking a ride?

cards.label: Bird with a berry
cards.why: A bird carries seeds to a new place.
cards.hint: Is it flower powder, or a seed taking a ride?

cards.label: Burrs on a sock
cards.why: The hooks stuck, so seeds can be carried away.
cards.hint: Did hooks stick and give something a ride?

cards.label: Hummingbird sipping from a flower
cards.why: Pollen rubs onto a hummingbird while it sips nectar, and it carries the pollen to the next flower.
cards.hint: is the animal carrying flower powder, or a seed?

cards.label: Wind blowing dandelion fluff
cards.why: Each fluffy parachute carries one seed away on the wind.
cards.hint: is the fluff carrying flower powder, or a seed?

stages.prompt: Which picture set counted this living thing? (Forest set: 6 kinds. Dune set: 3 kinds.)

cards.label: White-tailed deer
cards.why: The forest picture set counted the white-tailed deer.
cards.hint: think of where deer find leaves and trees to hide among.

cards.label: Robin
cards.why: The forest picture set counted the robin.
cards.hint: think of where a robin finds worms and a tree for its nest.

cards.label: Maple tree
cards.why: The forest picture set counted the maple tree.
cards.hint: think of a tree that turns red and orange in fall.

cards.label: Squirrel
cards.why: The forest picture set counted the squirrel.
cards.hint: think of where a squirrel finds acorns and tall trees.

cards.label: Beetle
cards.why: The forest picture set counted the beetle.
cards.hint: think of a small animal that lives under logs and leaves.

cards.label: Mushroom
cards.why: The forest picture set counted the mushroom.
cards.hint: think of what grows in the damp shade on forest logs.

cards.label: Beach grass
cards.why: The dune picture set counted beach grass.
cards.hint: think of a plant that holds sand in place.

cards.label: Gull
cards.why: The dune picture set counted the gull.
cards.hint: think of a bird that flies over sand and the lake shore.

cards.label: Insect
cards.why: The dune picture set counted an insect, so it had 3 kinds in all.
cards.hint: think of a small animal that crawls or flies near the sand.
